entities.summary:
The Battle of Aljubarrota, fought on August 14, 1385, was a pivotal clash between the Kingdom of Portugal and a Castilian army led by King John I of Castile. This decisive victory for the Portuguese, led by King John I, secured Portugal's independence from Castile and marked the beginning of a new era in Portuguese history.

The battle took place in the Leiria District, and its outcome was largely due to the superior tactics and bravery of the Portuguese knights. The Portuguese army, consisting of around 5,000 men, was outnumbered by the Castilian forces, but they managed to hold their ground and ultimately emerge victorious.

The aftermath of the Battle of Aljubarrota saw the rise of Portugal as a major power in the Iberian Peninsula. The victory marked the beginning of a golden age for Portugal, marked by significant cultural, artistic, and economic achievements. The battle also had significant consequences for the region, shaping the course of the Hundred Years' War and influencing the delicate balance of power in Europe.

The memory of the Battle of Aljubarrota has endured for centuries, with many considering it a turning point in Portuguese history.
